reconstructed_captions.34: A hand uses a sanding block to smooth the sealed edge of the leather.
reconstructed_captions.35: The hand applies another layer of sealing liquid to the leather edge for a smooth finish.
reconstructed_captions.36: A heated tool is used to polish and set the sealant on the leather edge.
reconstructed_captions.37: A wing divider is used to mark a consistent stitching line along the edge of the leather.
reconstructed_captions.38: A pricking iron is aligned with the marked line to prepare for punching holes.
reconstructed_captions.39: A mallet strikes the pricking iron, creating a row of stitching holes in the leather.
reconstructed_captions.40: The hand continues punching holes along the entire seam line.
reconstructed_captions.41: Two needles are threaded with white thread for the traditional saddle stitching technique.
reconstructed_captions.42: The hand-stitching process begins, passing needles through the first hole from opposite sides.
reconstructed_captions.43: A close-up shows the thread being pulled tight to create a durable saddle stitch.
reconstructed_captions.44: The stitching progresses steadily along the punched holes, joining the leather pieces.
reconstructed_captions.45: The final stitches are secured by backstitching, and the excess thread is trimmed off.
reconstructed_captions.46: A heated electric creasing tool is picked up to add a decorative finish.
reconstructed_captions.47: The tip of the creasing tool is carefully guided along the edge of the leather.
reconstructed_captions.48: The tool presses a clean, decorative line into the leather surface parallel to the seam.
